story.title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña Impeached and Arrested Amid Banking Crisis
story.summary: Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest following a banking crisis that left nearly three million customers unable to access their funds. The Senate voted unanimously for his removal over allegations related to the collapse of Ueno Bank. Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as the new president, pledging to compensate those affected by the crisis.

explore_lenses.label: What changed after Peña’s removal?
explore_lenses.title: Alliana completes the existing term
explore_lenses.summary: Congress removed Santiago Peña through impeachment, and Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in to serve the balance of the 2023–2028 term. The removal from office is distinct from the separate criminal investigation into alleged wrongdoing connected to Ueno Bank.

claims.text: The Senate declared Peña guilty of poor performance in office and removed him after a unanimous nominal vote of senators present.
Alliana took the presidential oath on November 6, 2026, to complete the 2023–2028 constitutional term; Congress then selected Antonio Barrios as vice president.

The Chamber of Deputies had approved impeachment charges by 78 votes, alleging conflicts of interest involving Ueno Holding, the central-bank appointment of a former Ueno executive, and the concentration of IPS funds at Ueno; these were impeachment allegations, not judicial findings of criminal guilt.

explore_lenses.label: When can Ueno customers access their money?
explore_lenses.title: An early payout law targets insured deposits
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate relief measure is not a blanket guarantee that every customer will be made whole at once. It creates an accelerated advance on deposit insurance, while the eventual recovery value of other deposits and bank securities depends on the resolution process.

claims.text: On November 4, Congress enacted an expedited advance of deposit insurance of up to 40 monthly minimum wages per depositor, with payment procedures to begin within 24 hours and not exceed five business days after the law takes effect.
The Senate’s account says the advance is calculated after offsetting a depositor’s overdue obligations to Ueno, and can be paid electronically or, if necessary, in cash.

A separate proposed measure authorizes the Central Bank to extend coverage to the full amount of specified public-sector deposits only for any balance not returned through ordinary resolution mechanisms; it does not establish identical full coverage for all private deposits.

The Central Bank’s securities regulator suspended trading in all Ueno-issued securities because recovery values depend on an assessment of the bank’s assets and liabilities that had not yet been determined.

story_report.summary: Paraguay’s Senate removed Santiago Peña from office and he was placed under house arrest as a banking crisis affecting nearly three million customers deepened. Pedro Alliana was sworn in to replace him, taking charge of the immediate political response while Congress moved to speed limited deposit-insurance payments for Ueno customers. The change of government does not settle questions over losses beyond insured deposits or potential criminal proceedings linked to the crisis.

sections.heading: Senate Removes Santiago Peña
sections.body: The Senate declared Peña guilty of poor performance in office and removed him in a unanimous nominal vote of those present. The Chamber of Deputies had approved the impeachment charges by 78 votes, citing alleged conflicts of interest involving Ueno Holding, the appointment of a former Ueno executive to the central bank and the concentration of IPS funds at Ueno. Those allegations formed the basis of impeachment proceedings and were not judicial findings of criminal guilt.

sections.heading: Alliana Completes Constitutional Term
sections.body: Alliana took the presidential oath on November 6, 2026, to complete the 2023–2028 constitutional term. Congress subsequently selected Antonio Barrios as vice president, establishing the new leadership arrangement after Peña’s removal.

sections.heading: Ueno Depositors Receive Accelerated Insurance
sections.body: Congress enacted an expedited advance of deposit insurance on November 4 of up to 40 monthly minimum wages per depositor. Procedures were to begin within 24 hours and payments were not to exceed five business days after the law took effect; amounts are calculated after offsetting overdue obligations to Ueno and may be paid electronically or in cash. Trading in Ueno-issued securities was suspended while authorities assess the bank’s assets and liabilities.

unresolved.text: The timing and outcome of any criminal case against Peña and other officials remain unresolved.
Official materials do not establish when uninsured Ueno deposits or the full value of claims on Ueno securities will be recovered.

related_stories.title: Jay Rockefeller, Former Governor and Senator, Passes Away at 89
related_stories.summary: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family's political dynasty, has died at the age of 89. He served as the governor of West Virginia and was a longtime U.S. senator, known for his advocacy on healthcare, education, and working families' needs. Rockefeller was born into a prominent family and forged a significant political career.

related_stories.title: Momentum Builds for Coalition Talks in Israel as Eisenkot Gains Support
related_stories.summary: Following inconclusive elections, opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot is gaining momentum in his efforts to form a government in Israel. He has received significant backing, including from Arab parties, as President Isaac Herzog prepares to announce who will be tasked with forming the new government. Eisenkot aims to replace long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

related_stories.title: ANC Faces Significant Decline in South African Local Elections
related_stories.summary: The African National Congress (ANC) is projected to receive less than a third of the vote in South Africa's local elections, marking a significant decline from previous years. With over 80% of ballots counted, the ANC is on track for its worst-ever election performance, estimated at around 32%. This decline is attributed to widespread voter dissatisfaction over issues such as water outages and power cuts, leading to potential coalition challenges in major cities like Johannesburg and Tshwane.

related_stories.title: New Zealand General Election Results Leave Parliament Divided
related_stories.summary: The New Zealand general election has concluded without a clear winner, resulting in a highly divided parliament. Preliminary results show the two main parties nearly deadlocked in the popular vote, leading to expectations of extended coalition negotiations. Minor parties, including the Opportunity Party, may play a crucial role in forming a government.
